study type: Qualitative (phenomenological) study, as part of a larger mixed-method study
exposure: Internal environmental factors (personal beliefs, self-confidence, lack of fear)
External environmental factors (spatial environment, social environment, interactive environment)
outcome: Ability to control/manage pain in labor
cohort: The study included 25 mothers who gave birth in four large hospitals in Iran, selected through stratified purposive sampling.
finding: Two major environmental factors (internal, comprising personal beliefs, self-confidence, and lack of fear; and external, comprising spatial, social, and interactive environments) were found to affect mothers' perception of pain and their ability to control it during labor.
mod_finding: N/A (The study's findings focus on pain management strategies rather than specific outcomes related to mode of birth, although it is contextualized by the high caesarean section rate due to labor pain and fear in Iran).
cross-section timing: Interviews were conducted with mothers who had given birth, focusing on their recent labor experience.
